summary: the prompt filename's stamp-first `.md` grammar is written in tickAttempt and depended on by renderedPrompts' listing filter and window compare; one home, read by the real readers

per.section: A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote

acceptance: One module composes a rendered prompt's filename, and it is the module whose readers depend on it: nothing outside `src/renderedPrompts.ts` spells the stamp-then-key-then-`.md` grammar, and `recordRenderedPrompt` takes it. The pins drive a real tick's own prompt file through the run-window trim and through the listing the outstanding-agent count reads, so a one-sided respell of the name reds. Behavior-free: no path written, no prompt kept, no count changed. `pnpm tsc --noEmit`, the suite, and the export and citation pins green.
pins: the run-window trim keeps a real tick's own rendered prompt and takes one written before the live run's claim
the rendered-prompt listing returns the file a real tick's writer left
notes: Verified on disk: writer src/tickAttempt.ts:909 (`${fsStamp()}-${slugify(key)}.md`); readers src/renderedPrompts.ts:102 (`.md` filter) and :71 (`name >= startStamp`, correct only because the stamp leads). The window and listing arms are driven only by hand-spelled names — tests/Dispatcher.test.ts:14538, :15533 (raw readdir), tests/cli.test.ts:2618. 1e801a5c pinned the prefix half of this seam; the name is the half left.
